title: Trace and base-change rearrangement before the first triangle
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $R_Z=\mathcal O_{E,Z}$ for the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring, $D(Z)=D(\Mod_{R_Z})$ for its unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and $\mathcal L(Z)=\Loc(\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E))$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible, sk-def-localizing-closure]. Pullbacks and direct images are the canonical derived functors with adjunction $h^*\dashv Rh_*$ [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction], and pullback coefficients are identified by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. All tensors are derived tensors over $R_Z$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For a proper $h:Z\to B$, let $\pi_{h,L,N}:L\otimes Rh_*N\to Rh_*(h^*L\otimes N)$ be the canonical projection map, the adjoint transpose of $1\otimes c_{h,N}$, where $c_h$ is the canonical counit.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper, let $W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], and use the canonical identification $fp_1=fp_2$. Put $T_Y=R_Y(1)[2]$, $T_X=f^*T_Y$, and $T_W=p_1^*T_X=p_2^*T_X$, with twists as in [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] and pullback/tensor comparisons as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Let $b_2:f^*Rf_*\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*$ and $b_1:f^*Rf_*\to Rp_{1*}p_2^*$ be the canonical base-change mates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Assume these and the projection maps used below are isomorphisms on $\mathcal L$ and that the displayed functors preserve $\mathcal L$. Take morphisms $t:Rf_*T_X\to R_Y$ and $t_i:Rp_{i*}T_W\to R_X$ satisfying $t_i\circ b_{i,T_X}=f^*t$ for $i=1,2$. Define $G(K)=f^*K\otimes T_X$ and
$$e_K=(1_K\otimes t)\circ\pi_{f,K,T_X}^{-1}:Rf_*GK\to K.$$
For $N\in\mathcal L(X)$ define the natural isomorphism
$$B_N:Rp_{2*}(p_1^*N\otimes T_W)\xrightarrow{\pi_{p_2,T_X,p_1^*N}^{-1}}Rp_{2*}p_1^*N\otimes T_X\xrightarrow{b_{2,N}^{-1}\otimes1}GRf_*N,$$
where the first arrow uses the canonical tensor symmetries.

For every $N\in\mathcal L(X)$ one has
$$e_{Rf_*N}\circ Rf_*(B_N)=Rf_*(1_N\otimes t_1)\circ Rf_*(\pi_{p_1,N,T_W}^{-1}).$$
The source of the left side is $Rf_*Rp_{2*}(p_1^*N\otimes T_W)$; that of the right side is identified with it by $Rf_*Rp_{2*}\simeq R(fp_2)_*=R(fp_1)_*\simeq Rf_*Rp_{1*}$. Both targets are $Rf_*N$.

proof.text: Work on small representatives of the pro-etale sites. The module operations are the ringed-topos operations: [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] derives the whole module pullback/direct-image composites, [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction] gives their canonical adjunction, and [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies the coefficient pullbacks and makes inverse image exact. Thus the ordinary unbounded ringed-topos comparisons apply with the actual sheaves $R_Z$. Use [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to suppress tensor and composition associators, preserving symmetry and the canonical adjunctions. Put $P=Rf_*$, $F=f^*$, $Q_i=Rp_{i*}$, $U_i=p_i^*$, $T=T_X$, $A=PN$, $C=PT$, $H=U_1N\otimes U_2T$, and $h=fp_1=fp_2$. In particular $U_1F=U_2F$, $U_1T=U_2T=T_W$, and $PQ_1=Rh_*=PQ_2$, with the adjunction-compatible comparisons specified by that node. Write $c_{u,E}$ for the canonical counit at $E$. All comparisons below take place in these ambient categories; the stated preservation and isomorphism hypotheses supply the maps needed on $\mathcal L$.

source.place: Tags 07A4, 0D6D, 07A6 and 0D6E: tensor, pullback composition, adjunction and direct-image composition

proof.text:
For a morphism $u$, write $\lambda_{u;E,L}:Ru_*E\otimes L\to Ru_*(E\otimes u^*L)$ for the projection map in direct-image-first order, obtained from the map $\pi_{u,L,E}$ defined in the statement using the two tensor symmetries. Its transpose is $c_{u,E}\otimes1$. Define two maps $A\otimes C\to Rh_*H$:
$$D_2=P(\lambda_{p_2;U_1N,T})\circ P(b_{2,N}\otimes1_T)\circ\pi_{f,A,T},$$
$$D_1=P(\pi_{p_1,N,T_W})\circ P(1_N\otimes b_{1,T})\circ\lambda_{f;N,C}.$$
Both are well typed: the intermediate targets in the first line are $P(FA\otimes T)$ and $P(Q_2U_1N\otimes T)$; in the second they are $P(N\otimes FC)$ and $P(N\otimes Q_1T_W)$. Naturality of symmetry and its compatibility with pullback are supplied by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. By the definition of $B_N$,
$$P(B_N)\circ D_2=\pi_{f,A,T}.$$
Consequently $D_2$ is an isomorphism by exactly the isomorphisms assumed in the item. No invertibility of the auxiliary map $\lambda_{f;N,C}$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map: the projection map and its transpose

proof.text:
Compute the transpose of $D_2$ under $h^*\dashv Rh_*$ by transposing first under $F\dashv P$ and then under $U_2\dashv Q_2$. These are the composite hom bijection by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. The adjunct-counit identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], applied to the defining projection maps, gives
$$(c_{p_2,U_1N}\otimes1)\circ(U_2b_{2,N}\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes U_2c_{f,T}).$$
Here the source is $U_2FA\otimes U_2FC=h^*(A\otimes C)$ and the target is $H$. The mate definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives
$$c_{p_2,U_1N}\circ U_2b_{2,N}=U_1c_{f,N}$$
under $U_2F=U_1F$. Substitution and bifunctoriality of tensor show that the displayed transpose is
$$\phi=(U_1c_{f,N})\otimes(U_2c_{f,T}).$$
This calculation uses naturality of the counits to transpose postcomposition; it is the explicit formula $c\circ L(\psi)$ in the cited adjunct identity.

Compute the transpose of $D_1$ using the other factorization $h=fp_1$. The same canonical composite-adjunction comparison and [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] give
$$(1\otimes c_{p_1,T_W})\circ(1\otimes U_1b_{1,T})\circ(U_1c_{f,N}\otimes1).$$
The mate characterization [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] now says
$$c_{p_1,T_W}\circ U_1b_{1,T}=U_2c_{f,T}.$$
The transpose is therefore again $\phi$, since $U_1FC=U_2FC$. The hom bijection for $h^*\dashv Rh_*$ is injective, so $D_1=D_2$ as maps to the same $Rh_*H$. In particular this equality uses the specified direct-image comparison, rather than an arbitrary identification of the two targets.

source.place: Tags 07A7 and 0B56; Categories Tag 0037: equality under the composite adjunction hom bijection

proof.text:
Precompose the left side of the required identity with $D_2$. The equality from step 2 and the definition of $e_A$ give
$$e_A\circ P(B_N)\circ D_2=e_A\circ\pi_{f,A,T}=1_A\otimes t.$$
Only cancellation of the specified inverse projection map is involved.

source.place: (1), first triangle: comparison with the defining counit

proof.text:
Precompose the right side with $D_1=D_2$ and cancel its $P(\pi_{p_1,N,T_W}^{-1})$ against the first factor of $D_1$. This gives
$$P(1_N\otimes t_1)P(\pi_{p_1,N,T_W}^{-1})D_1
=P(1_N\otimes(t_1b_{1,T}))\lambda_{f;N,C}
=P(1_N\otimes F(t))\lambda_{f;N,C}.$$
The second equality is exactly the hypothesis $t_1b_{1,T}=F(t)$, with $FR_Y=R_X$. Projection naturality in its scalar input, as stated by [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition], applied to $t:C\to R_Y$, identifies the last expression with
$$\lambda_{f;N,R_Y}\circ(1_A\otimes t)=1_A\otimes t.$$
The final equality is the tensor-unit normalization of the canonical projection map in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Both cited statements concern ordinary unbounded ringed-topos derived categories, so apply to the pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaves of step 1.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map: naturality and tensor-unit specialization

proof.text: Steps 5 and 6 show that the two maps in the statement agree after precomposition with the same isomorphism $D_2:A\otimes C\to Rh_*H$. Cancel $D_2$. With $A=Rf_*N$ and $PQ_2=Rh_*=PQ_1$ as fixed in step 1, this is precisely the asserted equality, with source and target as displayed in the item.

split_report.summary: Prove the trace rearrangement by comparing the two forward external-product composites under the canonical composite adjunction. Their explicitly computed transposes are the tensor of the pulled-back counits. Projection naturality and trace base change then prove the result after cancellation of the assumed isomorphism. Reuse existing ringed-topos coherence nodes; no new nodes and no statement changes.

Generic hom-bijection evaluation computes the two transposes explicitly; it is independent of the projective-line argument.
Only naturality of the canonical ordinary ringed-topos projection transformation is used to move t:C to R_Y.
Only its tensor-unit normalization is used at the final naturality calculation, with the actual pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaves.
